title: Quantization matrix: throughput vs. quality heatmap and regression guardrails
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a repeatable, statistically-sound benchmarking harness that produces a 2D matrix (quantization profile x workload shape) showing tokens/sec and quality deltas. Add automated regression detection and alerting so PRs or nightly runs flag CPU/GPU throughput or quality regressions introduced by quantization changes (FP16, INT8, INT4).
objective: Ship a canonical quantization benchmark that: (1) reports per-profile throughput (tokens/sec) and tail latencies (p95/p99) across representative workloads, (2) measures quality impact with deterministic and black-box metrics, and (3) raises meaningful regressions with low false-positive rate.
success_criteria: Heatmaps (CSV + PNG) produced nightly for all supported profiles: FP16, INT8-qsymmetric, INT8-qperchannel, INT4-w-o-activations
Automated regression checks run on PRs touching quantization code; any >10% throughput drop or >1.5% absolute quality degradation blocks merge unless explicitly approved
Dashboard in Console shows per-model/profile p95, tokens/sec, quality delta and historical control chart for last 30 runs
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark harness can be run locally and in CI with a single command (make quant-bench --profile=<profile> --workload=<workload>)
Results are emitted as flat CSV rows: model,profile,workload,seq_len,batch_size,tokens_sec,p50_ms,p95_ms,p99_ms,gen_cosine,bleu,wer,perplexity,seed
Regression detector implemented as a standalone step that returns non-zero exit code if thresholds are crossed; unit tests for detection logic included
Playbook updated: how to interpret heatmaps and triage quality vs perf trade-offs
benchmark_plan: Workloads: completion-short (avg 16 tokens), completion-medium (avg 128), chat-512 (user+assistant combined ~512), long-context (avg 2048) and embedding-bulk (batch embeddings 64x128-dim)
Sequence length distribution sampled to match production telemetry (weights: 50% short, 30% medium, 15% chat, 5% long)
Batch shapes: 1,2,4,8,16,32,64 to capture batching sensitivity
Concurrency sweep: 1,4,8,16,32 concurrent workers to capture latency/throughput knee
Cache states: cold-KV (first request), warm-KV (steady-state with cache hits), and prefix-caching scenarios for streaming workloads
Profiles: fp16, int8-symmetric, int8-perchannel, int4-weight-only, int4-activations-disabled
metrics_to_collect: quality metrics: embedding cosine similarity (vs FP32 baseline), BLEU/ROUGE for synthetic translation tasks, WER for ASR-style prompts, perplexity delta
statistical: mean, std, 95% bootstrap CI for tokens_sec and p95 latency
quality_thresholds: embedding cosine < 0.98 -> flag (verify with human eval subset)
Instruction-following regression (measured by instr-follow-automated harness) drop > 3% -> investigate
regression_detection: Baseline: last green nightly for the same model+seed+workload
Primary test: bootstrap CI overlap for tokens_sec and p95; if non-overlapping in direction of regression and relative change >= 10% then fail
Secondary test: Mann-Whitney U for latency distributions to detect shift in medians when bootstrap ambiguous
Multiple comparison correction: Benjamini-Hochberg at 0.05 across multiple workloads/profiles to limit FDR
EWMA control charts on p95 for continuous monitoring; trigger after 3 consecutive runs beyond 2-sigma
Action on fail: block PR (CI) or create regression incident (nightly) and attach heatmap + top-5 failing cases
Noise reduction: require n=5 repeated runs for noisy profiles before finalizing alert (configurable per-model)
test_harness_design: Harness implemented in Python with pluggable backends (local runtime, dedicated cluster runner, private VPC runner)
Runner produces a single newline-delimited JSON lines file per run (flat objects) to simplify ingestion into the analytics pipeline
Seeding: deterministic token generation and RNG seeds for decoding steps to reduce variance; separate runs with different seeds for robustness
Calibration: for INT8/INT4 we run calibration with a fixed 2k-sample dataset (representative prompts) and persist calibration tables alongside results
Warmup: 50 warmup inferences per worker to prime kernels/KV cache before measurement window
Telemetry hooks: use existing Console tracing agent for per-request metadata (route, model_version, profile, batch_size, seq_len)
tasks: Design CSV schema and heatmap generator (Liam)
Add calibration persistence and profile metadata to artifact store (Ravi)
Create CI job that runs PR-level smoke (subset of workloads) and nightly full matrix (Asha)
Integrate results into Console dashboard; add control charts and historical diff view (Design + Observability)
Write playbook and triage guide; add signal examples and runbook steps (PM)
notes: Trade-offs considered: running full matrix is expensive; adopt aggressive sampling for PRs (short+medium+embedding) and nightly full run for comprehensive coverage
INT4 with activation quantization shows good throughput gains but high variance in chat workloads; we will gate INT4 activation experiments behind a longer stability window
We prefer relative thresholds (percent) for throughput and absolute for certain quality metrics (WER, BLEU) to align with product tolerances

playbook: Interpreting a regression: look at the heatmap cell, then open the CSV to inspect per-sample failures. If quality flags and perf drops coincide, prioritize quality unless perf regression is >25%
Triage steps: reproduce locally with the same seed and calibration, run n=10 to confirm, open a regression incident and annotate with artifact links
Rollback guidance: provide model+profile+sha and recommend fallback profile (e.g., int8-perchannel -> fp16) in the incident ticket
